editorial.headline: Wood Building Components: Nationally Open, Bali Blocked
editorial.standfirst: This code covers wooden construction components, open nationally to 100% foreign ownership across all scales, but blocked for PMA registration in Bali under the province’s risk-class moratorium.
editorial.body:
This is a manufacturing activity built around wood as a construction material. The scope covers wooden building materials used mainly for construction: beams, rafters, roof frames finished on all four sides, and supporting posts made from finger-jointed wood with adhesive or connected with metal. It also reaches the more visible architectural elements of a building: doors, windows, shutters, frames, stairs, stair rails, wooden mouldings, wooden shingles, parquet blocks and strips assembled into panels from solid wood or engineering wood, decorative wall boards, and name boards.

The registration picture is broad at the national level. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scale businesses, so the code is not confined to one enterprise size. For PMA, the national position is also clear: the status is TERBUKA, the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%, and the cited source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Read nationally, that is a clean foreign-open classification, not a partial cap.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, placing it inside the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA, island-wide and permanently. The immediate planning consequence is simple: a foreign investor cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali under the record as written.

That distinction matters because the national rule and the Bali registration outcome point in opposite directions. Nationally, the activity is open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, the same activity is blocked for PMA registration because of the recorded risk-class moratorium. The honest reading is therefore not that the code is closed everywhere, and not that Bali has a separate percentage cap. The record gives one national ownership ceiling, then a Bali-side block based on status, reason, and moratorium rule.
